chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed Tamattu' on behalf of his mother and entered into Ihram for Hajj on behalf of his father, he (the Imam) said: 'If he slaughters the sacrificial animal, it is better for him; and if he does not slaughter, there is no penalty upon him, because he only performed Tamattu' on behalf of his mother and entered into Ihram for Hajj on behalf of his father.'

key_terms.أَهَلَّ: Entered into Ihram (ritual state for pilgrimage)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering the sacrificial animal when performing Hajj on behalf of parents with different rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on the sacrificial animal (Hady) when a person performs Tamattu' on behalf of his mother while entering Ihram for his father's Hajj. The Imam establishes that since the Tamattu' is specifically for the mother, the Hady is not strictly obligatory upon him; thus, slaughtering is recommended (khayr) but omitting it incurs no penalty, highlighting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding delegated Hajj obligations.
